# claude.md - Italian Law Crises (tree 274768699) ## Purpose Italian regulatory compliance control for ETG (Etraveli) call-center agents in Zendesk. Italian law requires call centers to tell Italian customers whether the handling agent is inside or outside the EU, and to offer transfer to an EU-based agent on request. This tree detects Italian customers, classifies the ticket, and surfaces the approved disclosure script (Giorgos Kasidis' EN + IT scripts) to the agent as a styled note card, then hands off to the Routing Tree. ## Architecture Flow: 7 -> 8 -> 5 -> 11 -> 1 -> 9 - Node 7 (Data, ROOT) "Edvin - Find Order": Connected Object 23 (http) - Edvin findOrder. Continues to 8. - Node 8 (Script) "Map Edvin Data": maps actions.findorder.phoneNumber -> customer_phone; Zendesk custom_field_27823498043154 -> order_number; sets agent_country (test: "GR" -- replace with real Zendesk agent lookup), brand/agent_first_name/city (test values -- replace with real brand + agent lookup), billing_country (test scaffolding -- Edvin's findOrder payload has no billing-address field, so this is derived from the same digit-normalized phone check node 5's classify() uses, kept in sync on purpose so the placeholder never disagrees with the real signal; replace with a real billing-country source when one exists). Guarded against a missing/failed Edvin response; ZT.logs its outputs. Continues to 5. - Node 5 (Script) "Classify & Render Disclosure" (formerly "Handle response"): now does BOTH jobs that used to be split across nodes 4 and 5. Reads customer_phone/billing_country/order_number/agent_country (form vars from node 8) and runs classify() -- a deterministic port of the old AI Action #14 rules (isItalian: phone digit-normalizes to a leading 39 or 0039 -- handles "+39 ...", "0039...", and a bare "39 3397874018" with no + or 00 prefix at all, the shape Edvin actually returns in production -- OR billing country is IT/Italy, case-insensitive; decided from customer data alone, never from agent_country, so a missing/unknown agent_country can never turn an Italian customer into "not applicable"; agentInEU: evaluated only when agent_country has a value, case-insensitive, is one of the 27 EU member codes -- a missing or unrecognized code is treated as outside-EU, which is the disclosure-COMPLETE branch, never the one that could suppress a required disclosure; orderSource: order_number begins with "40-" => bcom, else own_brand; scriptKey: eu_bcom/eu_own/noneu_bcom/noneu_own, or "" when applies=false). Publishes the six fields as form vars (italy_applies, italy_isItalian, italy_agentInEU, italy_isBcom, italy_orderSource, italy_scriptKey) for node 1's debug echo, then holds the SCRIPTS lookup table (the actual verbatim EN+IT text, four entries keyed by scriptKey) in code, builds the agent note card HTML, stores it via ZT.setTransformData('italy_note', html), and builds the Zendesk internal-note text via ZT.setTransformData('internal_note_details', ...) -- per Brent 2026-09-01 this note now carries only the header plus the actual EN/IT disclosure text the agent read (with ${brand}/${agent_first_name}/${city} tokens resolved by hand, since a Connected Object POST body never passes through Zingtree's content-node merge-field engine the way ${transforms.italy_note} does); the per-field audit dump (agent name, EU status, order source, matched key) was dropped as noise now that classify() is deterministic and auditable from the tree itself. Per Brent 2026-09-02: formatting matches the ETG "Register Errands - Dynamic" tree's node 21 "Format Internal Note" exactly, since that node posts through the same Connected Object 57 and is proven correct in production -- **bold** markdown (not HTML tags) for the English:/Italian: labels, \n\n between blocks for the blank-line spacing, and JSON.stringify(...).slice(1,-1) to escape the string for the Connected Object body instead of a hand-rolled replace() escaper. Fails closed with a visible warning if scriptKey doesn't match a known key (defensive backstop only now -- classify() cannot itself produce an unknown key). Continues to 11. - Node 11 (Data) "Create Internal Note": Connected Object 57 (http), posts transforms.internal_note_details as a Zendesk internal note. Continues to 1. - Node 1 (Content) "Start Node": debug echo of the classification (${italy_applies} etc. -- form vars set by node 5) + ${transforms.italy_note} card. Button -> 9. - Node 9 (Tree) "Routing Tree": opens tree 606991820. - Node 10 (Content, UNLINKED) -- this claude.md memory node. Never part of the flow. ## Data dictionary - Inbound: Zendesk custom_field_27823498043154 (order number). - Form vars: customer_phone, order_number, billing_country, agent_country, brand, agent_first_name, city (all set in node 8); italy_applies, italy_isItalian, italy_agentInEU, italy_isBcom, italy_orderSource, italy_scriptKey (all set in node 5, replacing the old actions.italy_region_compliance.* output). - Transforms: italy_note (HTML card; producer node 5, consumer node 1), internal_note_details (Zendesk internal-note text -- markdown, matching the ETG "Register Errands - Dynamic" tree's node 21 convention: **bold** labels, \n\n blank-line spacing, JSON.stringify(...).slice(1,-1) escaping; header + the EN/IT script actually read, or a one-line "not applicable"/escalation note; producer node 5, consumer node 11). - actions.findorder - Connected Object 23, Edvin findOrder (phoneNumber used). ## External systems - Edvin findOrder via Connected Object 23 (data_connected_object_type http) on node 7. - Zendesk internal-note post via Connected Object 57 (data_connected_object_type http) on node 11, fed by transforms.internal_note_details. CO 57 is the same "Zendesk - Add Internal Note" object the ETG "Register Errands - Dynamic" tree posts through (its node 22, fed by node 21 "Format Internal Note") -- that tree's node 21 is the reference for how CO 57 actually renders text (markdown **bold**, not HTML), used here 2026-09-02. - AI Action #14 "Italy - EU Agent Region Disclosure" (alias italy_region_compliance, google/gemini-2.5-flash, connector 54) is RETIRED as of 2026-09-01 -- see Changelog. It is no longer referenced by any node in this tree. It still exists as an account-level AI Action record; deactivate/delete it in Zingtree admin separately if it isn't used elsewhere (this JSON edit alone cannot do that). ## Conventions & gotchas - **Why this is a script, not an AI Action (2026-09-01 architecture change):** the three rules (phone/billing prefix check, EU-list membership, order-number prefix check) are pure deterministic boolean/string logic with no judgment call involved -- exactly the case the AI Action's own Instructions field already argued didn't need a model ("You are a deterministic rule evaluator... Apply ONLY the rules provided"). Routing it through an LLM anyway meant identical inputs could occasionally classify differently between runs (sampling variance the prompt's "be deterministic" instruction cannot fully suppress), which is unacceptable for a regulatory disclosure gate. Replacing it with a script removes the non-determinism entirely, plus the latency, per-call cost, and prompt-injection surface (customer phone/order number no longer get concatenated into an LLM context at all). See the 8/31 changelog entries below for why the AI Action existed in the first place and the two edits that worked around its Instructions-field editor limitations -- none of those limitations apply to a script node, which is why the fix is a straight removal rather than another workaround. - **Confirmed deviation from the old AI Action's literal fail-closed wording (2026-09-01, confirmed with Brent):** the AI Action's instructions said "if any input needed for a decision is missing or unclear... treat the requirement as not applying" as a blanket rule. Taken literally for a missing/unrecognized agent_country, that would mean applies=false even when the customer IS Italian -- i.e. silently skipping a required disclosure. classify() does NOT do that: applies/isItalian are decided from the customer's own data only (phone + billing country) and never look at agent_country at all. agent_country is evaluated only when a value is present, and only to choose eu_* vs noneu_* for a ticket that already applies -- an unknown/unrecognized agent_country falls to "outside EU" for scriptKey purposes (the branch that ADDS the "you may request an EU agent" offer rather than omitting it, i.e. still disclosure-complete). agentKnown is tracked separately so node 5's card still warns the agent when location wasn't confirmed. This is confirmed, intended behavior, not an open question. - **Phone-format bug fixed 2026-09-01:** Edvin's phoneNumber field is not consistently "+39"/"0039"-prefixed -- production data has come back as a bare "39 3397874018" with no + and no 00 trunk prefix at all. The original rule (and the AI Action before it) only matched a literal "+39"/"0039" prefix, so a real Italian customer with this phone shape classified as not Italian and the card silently rendered the empty "na" state instead of the disclosure. This is very likely the real explanation for the original "same input, different result" complaint too: a bare "39 ..." number doesn't cleanly satisfy a literal "+39/0039" instruction, so the old AI Action was left to use judgment on exactly this kind of input -- and judgment calls are where sampling variance shows up. Fix: isItalianPhone() in node 5 strips every non-digit character (space, dash, dot, parens, +) before checking for a leading "39" or "0039" -- no other ITU calling code is "39", so this is unambiguous for a field that is always country-code-first. Node 8's billing_country test-scaffolding uses the identical normalization so it can never disagree with node 5. Regression-tested against the real production payload plus a case that only contains "39" mid-string (must NOT match). - **Script node source must still be pure ASCII** (Zingtree script engine constraint -- "curly quotes and unicode break scripts"). Node 5 writes the Italian accented character as a ò escape (`puo` with an accent) so the SOURCE stays ASCII while the runtime STRING still contains the real character. Never paste a literal accented character into a script node; always use its \uXXXX escape. - Placeholders in the approved scripts use Zingtree merge-field syntax (${brand}, ${agent_first_name}, ${city}) so Zingtree fills them from session variables. Node 8 sets test values (brand=ETG, agent_first_name=Agent, city=Athens) until real sources exist. - Order source rule: order number starting "40-" = Booking.com ("bcom"); otherwise own_brand (= "ETG" in Giorgos' script table). - Node 8 hardcodes agent_country="GR" (two-letter code), brand/agent_first_name/city test values, and derives billing_country from a +39/0039 prefix check (via includes(), see note above) -- all test scaffolding pending real sources (Zendesk agent lookup by agent_email for agent_country/city/agent_first_name; a real billing-country source; a real brand source). Node 8 is guarded against a missing/failed Edvin findorder response and ZT.logs its outputs for Execution Insights. - If the card shows "Not applicable" unexpectedly, check Execution Insights for the "italy inputs:" log line (node 8) -- an empty phone usually means Edvin findOrder failed (the ETG test server's DB rebuild schedule causes evening 500s per MEMORY.md). - Known typos in the approved Italian text, inserted as provided pending ETG confirmation: "chiderle" (likely "chiederle"), "trasferita un agente" (likely "trasferita a un agente"). ## Changelog - 2026-08-28 - Brent via Claude - Inserted Giorgos' approved EN+IT disclosure scripts into AI Action #14's four empty script slots; rewrote node 5 to render the returned script verbatim; added this claude.md node - AI Action #14 config, nodes 5, 10. - 2026-08-31 (pass 1) - Brent via Claude - Zingtree's editor stripped the angle-bracket placeholders from the first paste -- reissued the AI Action #14 Instructions split into system + user blocks with ${brand}/${agent_first_name}/${city} merge-field placeholders; node 8 hardened (no throw on missing findorder, agent_country "GR" code, begins-with +39/0039 check, ZT.log debug line); node 5 handles a single-line "EN: ... IT: ..." script - AI Action #14 config, nodes 5, 8. - 2026-08-31 (pass 2) - Brent via Claude - AI Action's Instructions field rejected the Italian accented character outright (content-validation error). Redesigned so the AI Action never carries script text at all: it now outputs a scriptKey enum (eu_bcom/eu_own/noneu_bcom/noneu_own/empty), and node 5 holds the verbatim EN+IT scripts in a SCRIPTS lookup table in code (ASCII source, ò escape for the accented character). Node 1's debug echo updated to include scriptKey - AI Action #14 config, nodes 1, 5. - 2026-09-01 - Brent via Claude - AI Action #14 was non-deterministic in production (same inputs, different classifications across runs) -- unacceptable for a regulatory disclosure gate, and the rules it evaluated never needed a model in the first place (all three are deterministic boolean/string checks, as the AI Action's own Instructions already stated). Deleted node 4 (AI Action) entirely; merged its classify() logic into node 5 as plain JS, ported 1:1 from AI Action #14's Instructions field plus a deliberate fail-safe deviation (see Conventions above -- unknown agent_country now falls to the disclosure-complete branch instead of silently marking applies=false). Node 5 now publishes italy_applies/italy_isItalian/italy_agentInEU/italy_isBcom/italy_orderSource/italy_scriptKey as form vars; node 1's debug echo repointed from ${actions.italy_region_compliance.*} to these. Node 8's continuation repointed from 4 to 5. Flow is now 7 -> 8 -> 5 -> 11 -> 1 -> 9. Verified classify() against a 12-case matrix (EU/non-EU agent, bcom/own-brand, Italian/non-Italian, missing/unrecognized agent_country, missing order_number, phone-substring-not-prefix guard, case-insensitivity) before shipping -- AI Action #14 config, nodes 1, 5, 8, 10; node 4 deleted. - 2026-09-01 (follow-up) - Brent via Claude - Confirmed with Brent: applies/isItalian must never fall back to "not applicable" just because agent_country is missing. classify() already worked this way (isItalian/applies are decided from phone+billing only; agent_country is evaluated only when present, and only to choose eu_* vs noneu_*) -- updated comments in node 5 and this file from "flagged for review" to "confirmed" to reflect that this is settled, intended behavior, not an open question - node 5, nodes 10. - 2026-09-01 (bugfix) - Brent via Claude - Real production data (an actual Zendesk/Edvin session dump) showed a live Italian customer classifying as not Italian: Edvin's phoneNumber came back as a bare "39 3397874018" with no + and no 00 prefix, which the +39/0039-only prefix check missed entirely, so the disclosure card silently rendered the empty "na" state. Very likely the real explanation for the original AI-Action non-determinism too. Fixed classify() in node 5 to strip non-digit characters and match a leading "39" or "0039" (isItalianPhone()/normalizedDigits()), and synced node 8's billing_country test-scaffolding to the same check so it can't disagree. Added 3 regression tests (the real payload, a punctuated variant, and a "39 mid-string must not match" guard) -- 15/15 passing - nodes 5, 8, 10. - 2026-09-01 (internal note) - Brent via Claude - Per Brent: the internal note should carry the EN/IT disclosure script the agent read, not the per-field audit dump. Rewrote node 5's note builder: header + (not-Italian: one line / Italian: the actual English/Italian script text, merge-fields resolved by hand since a Connected Object POST body never passes through Zingtree's content-node merge-field engine / no-match: an escalation line, defensive-only) -- dropped Agent/Italian contact/Disclosure required/Agent location/Order source/Matched script key. Also fixed g() to always pass an explicit default (patterns.md rule) while touching this code. Surfaced a pre-existing gap while verifying end-to-end: agent_first_name is referenced by the SCRIPTS text and by this note but is never actually set anywhere in the tree (node 8 sets city/agent_country/brand, not agent_first_name, despite claude.md previously claiming it did as a test value) -- both the agent-facing card and now this note render it blank until a real source is wired in; flagged, not fixed, since the right fallback/source is a product call, not a refactor. Verified end-to-end against the real production payload -- node 5. - 2026-09-02 (internal note formatting) - Brent via Claude - Per Brent: bold the "English:"/"Italian:" labels in the internal note and put a blank line between the two script lines. Since plain text cannot render bold, internal_note_details is now built as HTML ( labels,
joins instead of \n, blank line between the EN and IT lines) rather than plain text; the ${brand}/${agent_first_name}/${city} substitutions are now HTML-escaped since they land inside markup. FLAGGED, not fully verifiable from here: this only renders as bold in Zendesk if Connected Object 57 posts internal_note_details into the html_body comment field -- if it currently posts to the plain-text body field, the /
tags will show up as literal text in the ticket. CO 57's request template lives outside this tree JSON, so confirm/update the field mapping in Zingtree's Connected Objects admin before treating this as done - node 5. - 2026-09-02 (internal note formatting, corrected) - Brent via Claude - Brent pointed at the ETG "Register Errands - Dynamic" tree's internal note (node 21 "Format Internal Note" -> node 22, PRODUCTION 2026-08-27 v2 export) as the reference: it posts through the same Connected Object 57 and is confirmed correctly formatted in production. Replaced the previous pass's HTML/ guess with node 21's actual convention: **bold** markdown (not HTML tags) for the English:/Italian: labels, \n\n between blocks for the blank line, \n within a block for a plain break, and JSON.stringify(internal_note_details).slice(1, -1) to escape the string instead of a hand-rolled replace() chain -- matches node 21 exactly. This also resolves the previous entry's open question about which Zendesk field CO 57 posts into: node 21's production behavior proves it renders markdown, not raw HTML, so the earlier html_body/ approach was the wrong mechanism regardless of field mapping - node 5.
10.notes: In-tree memory file for AI-assisted maintenance. Not part of the flow.
